A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LR-QR work and provide readable text, equations, figures, and appendices. The complete 33-page v1 and 34-page v2 support comparison, including matching the relocated RxRx1 experiment and theoretical proofs.

before.justification: Sections 5.2–5.3 report original coverage and prediction-set-size results on Communities and Crime and RxRx1. Appendix B reports a regularization ablation.

after.justification: Sections 5.2–5.3 report Communities and Crime and new MMLU results. Original RxRx1 results and the regularization ablation remain in Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: The population and empirical LR-QR objectives, joint optimization over the threshold and scalar, and prediction-set construction remain equivalent. Section 3 changes the explanation, while the ten-candidate, three-fold regularization-selection procedure remains unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds MMLU multiple-choice question answering, extending coverage to language models and a difficulty-based shift from elementary/high-school subjects to college/professional subjects. Communities and Crime and all 14 RxRx1 scenarios remain; RxRx1 moves to Appendix B.

E2.justification: V2 adds DR-iso from Gui et al. (2024) and Robust-CP from Ai and Ren (2024) to the four existing baselines. Their participation is verified in the RxRx1 plots and MMLU Table 1. Both works were cited in v1 but were not evaluated there.

E3.justification: The added MMLU evaluation introduces Llama 13B next-token scoring over four answer options and the nonconformity score 1 minus the correct-answer probability. Existing Communities and Crime and RxRx1 splits, predictors, scoring rules, metrics, and regularization-validation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: The regularization sweep and held-out-gradient analysis retain the same setup, findings, and plotted curves, moving from v1 Appendix B/Figure 4 to v2 Appendix C/Figure 3. MMLU adds benchmark evidence without a separate new ablation or diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report 1000 random splits for Communities and Crime, 50 for RxRx1, and 100 for the ablation, with the same error-bar reporting practice. MMLU introduces point estimates without additional run-count, confidence-interval, or significance-test reporting.

E6.justification: New MMLU Table 1 reports LR-QR coverage of 89.6% and set size 3.38, versus DRO's 99.7% and 3.92. DR-iso and Robust-CP results are added, and DRO-CP set sizes change in matched RxRx1 plots under the retained stated protocol. V1's RxRx1 coverage-deviation summary and aggregate set-size bars are removed. V2 Figure 1's legend error makes its method-specific changes ambiguous.

T1.justification: V2 adds Corollary 4.4, an indicator-basis specialization asserting group-conditional coverage bounds. It also explicitly requires positive regularization in the main results and changes Theorem 4.3's final coverage-error remainder from a Theta expression to an explicit term. The main generalization rates and appendix derivations are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list extend the empirical outperformance claim to MMLU question answering. The central claims of avoiding direct likelihood-ratio estimation and obtaining controlled marginal-coverage error through stability analysis remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3 newly explains the scalar beta through likelihood-ratio normalization, replacing the earlier reparametrization-focused motivation. V2 interprets MMLU results as demonstrating validity and efficiency among methods with approximately nominal coverage. Existing misspecification limitations and regularization tradeoffs remain.

D1.justification: Section 5.3 adds MMLU implementation information: the prompt suffix, answer-token logit processing, GPT-2 Small's 768-dimensional embeddings, token averaging, and logistic likelihood-ratio estimation. Existing implementation descriptions and the code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Kumar et al. (2023) to motivate the LLM scoring scheme and expands the method's connection to existing quantile-regression work. Gibbs et al. (2025) is the published version of an already cited work; Gui et al. and Ai and Ren were already discussed in v1.

P1.justification: Section 3 is substantially rewritten, replacing five subsections with a more direct hypothesis-class and normalization narrative followed by the algorithm. RxRx1 moves from the main experiments to Appendix B, MMLU occupies Section 5.3, and mathematical exposition and terminology are streamlined throughout.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 1 and redraws comparison plots with additional series, revised axes and legends, and vertically stacked full RxRx1 panels. It also introduces a material Figure 1 legend defect: the dashed nominal-coverage line is labeled LR-QR, method labels are misassigned, and the pink bars lack a legend entry.

improvement.justification: MMLU and the additional robust baselines broaden empirical support, and the rewritten method exposition is more direct. However, v1's interpretable Communities and Crime legend becomes misassigned in v2 Figure 1, compromising method-specific comparisons, while useful RxRx1 aggregate summaries disappear. The PDFs do not resolve the intended bar identities, so the evidential gains and reporting losses leave the net quality change uncertain.
